name: Massachusetts
tagline: From Cape Cod's bay shore to Mount Greylock, by Quabbin and the Mohawk Trail.
intro: Massachusetts byways run from the bay side of Cape Cod and the North Shore harbors through the Revolutionary country around Concord and the Quabbin hills to the farms of the Connecticut Valley and the Berkshire summits. This chapter follows the fourteen state scenic byways mapped by the Massachusetts Department of Transportation, which keeps no published list of its own beyond that map and GIS layer, and whose roads were designated one at a time, the Battle Road for instance by an act of the legislature in 2006. Four of them, the Battle Road, the Mohawk Trail, the Old King's Highway and the Connecticut River route, also carry national designation.

members.name: Battle Road
members.blurb: About fourteen miles of Massachusetts Avenue and North Great Road from Arlington through Lexington and Lincoln to Concord, near the line British regulars marched on April 19, 1775, ending by the Buttrick Mansion in Minute Man National Historical Park.

members.name: Blackstone Canal Heritage Highway
members.blurb: Route 122 follows the Blackstone River from Grafton through Northbridge, Uxbridge and Millville to the Rhode Island line, past mill villages in the valley where canal boats ran between Worcester and Providence from 1828 to 1848.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Chappaquiddick Road
members.blurb: Chappaquiddick's main paved road crosses the island off Edgartown's eastern end through red cedar woods and salt marsh, giving out onto sandy woodland tracks to the shore. Mytoi, a small Japanese garden, sits in the brush nearby.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Connecticut River Scenic Farm Byway
members.blurb: Routes 47 and 63 follow the Connecticut River from South Hadley to Northfield through Hadley's farmland and old village centers, passing Sunderland's Buttonball Tree, a sycamore already alive when the Constitution was signed.

members.name: Essex Coastal Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Some ninety miles of North Shore road run from Lynn to Salisbury, past Ipswich's cluster of First Period houses and the marshes of Essex, where fifteen shipyards built one in every 28 American ships in 1852.

members.name: Jacob's Ladder Trail
members.blurb: US 20 between Lee and Russell, billed as the country's first auto road over a mountain range, climbs to a stone cairn at 1,775 feet on Morey Hill in Becket, raised by a crowd of motorists in 1910.

members.name: Lost Villages Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 122 runs forty miles from Orange to Paxton along the north side of the Quabbin Reservoir, whose building in the 1930s forced four towns to move. Gates in Petersham still lead to the old Dana common and Greenwich.

members.name: Minuteman Highway
members.blurb: Route 2 from Cambridge through Arlington, Belmont and Lexington to the Concord Rotary, a divided highway running parallel to the Battle Road and just south of it, near Minute Man National Historical Park.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mohawk Trail
members.blurb: Routes 2 and 2A follow an old Native American trade route over the Hoosac Range, opened to motorists in 1914, crossing the French King Bridge high above the Connecticut and dropping by a hairpin turn into North Adams.

members.name: Mount Greylock Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Reservation roads climb from Lanesborough farmland to Mount Greylock's 3,491-foot summit, with its 1932 War Memorial Tower and CCC-built Bascom Lodge, then descend to North Adams. Cars may use them from late May to mid-October.

members.name: Old King's Highway
members.blurb: Route 6A runs along Cape Cod's bay side from Bourne to Orleans through eight National Register districts, past early Cape houses and sea captains' homes, with cranberry bogs and bayside marsh in view.

members.name: Route 112 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 112 runs from the Vermont line at Colrain south to Huntington through hill farms with honor-system stands, passing Shelburne Falls, where the Bridge of Flowers blooms April to October, and following the Westfield River's east branch.

members.name: Route 116 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 116 crosses the hills from Adams to South Deerfield by way of Cheshire, which once sent President Jefferson a 1,234-pound wheel of cheese, and Conway, home of the 1870 Burkeville covered bridge.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Taconic Trail
members.blurb: Route 2 climbs west from US 7 in Williamstown through the Taconic Trail state forest to Petersburg Pass on the New York line, a short, winding crossing of the Taconic Range that keeps its name into New York.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).
